question: Can the Constitution override a federal tax statute?
answer: Under Article 8 of the Constitution of Pakistan, any law, including a federal tax statute, that is inconsistent with the rights conferred by the Constitution shall, to the extent of such inconsistency, be void. This means that if a federal tax statute contradicts a fundamental right protected by the Constitution, the Constitution will override the tax statute. In simple terms, the Constitution has higher authority than any other law, including tax laws.
